item: row 339 (R800) and R801: trust decisions from another installation's backup, or one signed with a key a restore placed, need a click
key_paths: src/backup/merge.py; src/annotations/store.py; src/api/annotations.py; src/reporting/evidence.py; src/backup/artifact.py; src/backup/stream_backup.py; src/static/app-home.js; src/static/oo-on.js; tests/test_merge_imported_annotations.py; tests/test_restored_key_marker_r801.py
summary: a restore applies imported authors' trust flags automatically only from an artifact signed with this installation's own key; from any other verified key the authors import untrusted with a trust_withheld marker naming that key, the report counts and lists them, and the web-of-trust list asks once per key with the fingerprint, the count and the author names, No focused first; Import them applies them only while the same authors are still the ones shown (else 409, nothing changed); an annotations member is routed on its normalised name and only annotations/mine.json and annotations/imported/<id>.json are restored, any other name refused (security reads: annotations/./imported/x.json wrote its trust flag past the gate); R801: while this installation has no evidence key a restore writes a marker beside it before placing any key file, kept whenever an evidence key exists after the restore placed one (whatever spelling it was carried under; another case, a trailing dot or space of a key or marker name is refused), and while any marker exists is_this_installations_key (the one check R795's verdict and row 340's signer relation now ask) says another installation; only a new key of this installation's own removes it, a backup never places or removes one; a key an older build restored cannot be recognised (import reports travel in backups and could demote the installation's own key), so it keeps counting as its own; the trust click must name the authors it showed; strings x12.
